content.text:
I identify the sample as a single phase, CaSmAlO4 (mp-1227060). I simulated all nine candidates and compared their peaks with the observed pattern by eye; I did not fit the patterns numerically.

- **CaSmAlO4 matches the peak sequence.** Its simulated pattern has peaks near 14.65, 25.3, 29.3, 32.5, 33.9 and 38°, followed by a cluster of peaks between 45 and 72°. The observed peaks follow the same sequence with similar relative intensities: 14.8, 25.4, 29.5, 32.4, 33.6, 38.2, 46.85, 51.8, 59–64, 69.1 and 71.3°.
- **The fit is not exact.** Observed peaks sit about 0.1–0.3° away from the simulated ones, and not always in the same direction, which is consistent with strain. The two strongest peaks also swap order: the simulation puts 32.5° highest, but in the data 33.6° is highest.
- **The other layered candidate is ruled out.** Eu3Al2O7 has no strong peak near 14.8°, which is one of the strongest observed peaks. It also predicts a strong peak near 24.7° that is missing from the data.
- **No second phase is needed.** The remaining candidates put strong peaks where the observed pattern is only background, and none is needed to explain any extra peaks.
